lesson.text: Quick memory: what is profit? (Money in take away money out.) Today: a shop's harder days.
When a cost goes up, a fair price goes up a little. Tell customers why: honesty keeps their trust.
Make what customers will buy. On a rainy day bake less: bread nobody buys is money wasted.
A big order is a promise. If something goes wrong, tell the customer early and agree a new plan.
A fair wage is the hours worked times the rate for each hour. Pay it in full and on time.
Never sell below what it costs to beat a rival, and never use tricks. Save part of the profit to grow.
Try it in the practice room: get your bakery through its harder days.

exercises.prompt: Flour gets dearer. A fair price...
choices: goes up a little, and you say why
exercises.explain: It goes up a little, and you say why.

exercises.prompt: Bread nobody buys is money wasted.
Rain halves your customers. You bake...
A loaf cost 2 coins to make. Flour goes up by 1. What does it cost now?
Bobo works 3 hours at 3 coins an hour. His wage?
10 honey buns at 2 coins each. The total?
The honey for a big order comes late. You...
choices: tell the customer early and agree a plan
leave the honey out and say nothing
exercises.explain: Tell them early: you fix it together.

exercises.prompt: A rival sells bread below what it costs. You...
choices: keep a fair price and good quality
exercises.explain: Below the cost can't last; quality can.

exercises.prompt: Someone who never visited writes "Not a nice bakery". You...
You save 30 coins a month for an oven costing 120. How many months?
Giving back to your village can be part of a successful business.
exercises.explain: True: good businesses help people too.
